name: Canyonlands National Park
blurb: Soil crust, kangaroo rats and lions in a canyon desert cut by two rivers.

tip.title: Take away the rain
tip.text: Set Rain & snowmelt to -100% and watch the soil crust and grasses fade, then the seed-eaters, then the coyotes and lions that live on them.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: A living skin of cyanobacteria, lichens and mosses on desert soil. It binds soil against erosion and some of its cyanobacteria fix nitrogen, but footsteps can break it up and recovery is very slow.
A low, dense desert shrub of the Colorado Plateau, browsed by deer and bighorn sheep.
A drought-tolerant tree of the pinyon-juniper woodland on the mesas. Its foliage and berry-like cones feed deer and squirrels.
A small pine whose large seeds are a key food for jays, squirrels and mice in the woodland.
The most-recorded mammal in the park area. A nocturnal seed-eating rodent that is prey for foxes, coyotes and owls.
A small, nocturnal, omnivorous rodent, widespread and abundant, that eats seeds and insects and feeds many predators.
A large ground squirrel of rocky canyon country that eats seeds, nuts and juniper berries.

nodes.name: Desert bighorn sheep
nodes.desc: A sure-footed grazer and browser of the canyon rims and cliffs, and a prey of mountain lions.
A crepuscular browser that eats shrubs and grasses and feeds lions, coyotes and scavengers.
An omnivorous canid of rocky, wooded canyons that takes mice, birds, and carrion.
The most-recorded bird in the park area. An intelligent omnivore that scavenges carrion.

nodes.name: Turkey vulture
nodes.desc: A soaring scavenger that feeds on carcasses and cleans up dead animals across the canyons.
A flexible, dawn-and-dusk predator of rodents and deer that also takes carrion.

nodes.name: Mountain lion
nodes.desc: A mostly nocturnal ambush predator of the canyons that hunts deer and bighorn sheep.
Powers both the crust and plants of an open, sunlit landscape.
Scarce, irregular water drives plant growth and crust activity in this arid plateau.
Fungi, bacteria and invertebrates that recycle dead plants and animals into the soil.
